Ret_UncuedReconstruct.name: Uncued Reconstruct
Ret_UncuedReconstruct.description: Word bank slots, formula fill, or scrambled clause assembly - the learner rebuilds the answer from scratch with no cues.
Ret_UncuedReconstruct.bestFor: Verbal/syntactic learners; low working memory load

schema.title: Ret_UncuedReconstruct
schema.description: Uncued Reconstruct: the learner rebuilds a target from scratch by assembling chunks (words, formula terms, or clauses) into ordered slots, with no cues given. Supports word-bank / formula-fill / scrambled-clause modes through a single slot-plus-bank interaction.

title.description: Short activity heading shown at the top of the block.

prompt.description: Instruction line telling the learner what to reconstruct (no answer content).

context.description: Optional stimulus text (quotation, scenario, derivation context) displayed above the slots.

contextLabel.description: Optional small caption for the context block, e.g. 'The Gettysburg Address, para. 2'.

answerLabel.description: Optional caption over the slot row, e.g. 'Reconstructed sentence' or 'Kinetic energy'.

placeholder.description: Optional placeholder text shown inside empty slots.

items.description: One or more reconstruction rounds, presented one at a time.

context.description: Optional round-specific context override; falls back to the block-level context.

chunks.description: Pieces available in the bank and used to fill the slots. Chunks whose text equals a solution entry are correct in that slot; all others act as distractors.

text.description: Exact text of the chunk (plain text; may contain math-ish symbols like ΔG° or ½mv²).

ariaLabel.description: Optional screen-reader-friendly reading of the chunk.

solution.description: The correct ordered sequence of chunk texts; its length sets the number of slots.

correct.description: Message shown when the learner's arrangement matches the solution exactly.

partial.description: Message shown when some but not all positions are right.

incorrect.description: Message shown when nothing is in its right position.

explanation.description: Short rationale revealed with the feedback.

feedback.description: Optional block-level default feedback strings used when a round omits them.

completeMessage.description: Optional message shown once every round has been reconstructed correctly.

Ret_SpeedCategorizer.name: Speed Categorizer
Ret_SpeedCategorizer.description: Rapid binary swipes or 3-way bucket sorting under a timer.

schema.title: Speed Categorizer
schema.description: Rapid bucket-sorting drill under a timer. Cards arrive one at a time and the learner taps (or swipes) them into buckets as fast as possible.

title.description: Drill title shown in the header.

prompt.description: Short instruction line telling the learner what to do.

seconds.description: Total time for the drill in seconds.

showExplanations.description: When true, the card's explanation flashes after it is sorted. Defaults to true.

buckets.description: 2 or 3 destination buckets, in display order.

label.description: Bucket label shown on its button.

shortLabel.description: Optional compact label used on wide-layout quick keys.

hint.description: Optional one-line reminder shown under the bucket label.

cards.description: The deck. Cards are served in the given order.

text.description: The card face: the item the learner must categorize.

detail.description: Optional secondary line under the card text.

correctBucket.description: id of the bucket this card belongs to.

explanation.description: Optional line shown briefly after the card is sorted.

Ret_MisconceptionTrap.name: Misconception Trap
Ret_MisconceptionTrap.description: A choice among plausible, highly tempting flawed options - only one survives scrutiny.
Ret_MisconceptionTrap.bestFor: High-confidence learners who skim or pattern-match

schema.title: Misconception Trap
schema.description: A single-choice challenge built from tempting, plausible flawed options where exactly one answer survives scrutiny. The learner taps one option; the trap they chose is marked as a misconception and the surviving answer is revealed with its reasoning.

prompt.description: The question or claim the learner must judge.

text.description: Wording of the option, as the learner sees it.

whyNot.description: Why this option is tempting but flawed (or, for the correct option, why it survives scrutiny). Shown after the choice is locked in.

correctId.description: The id of the single option that survives scrutiny.

successMessage.description: Short verdict line shown when the learner picks the surviving option (e.g. 'Survives scrutiny').

notQuiteMessage.description: Short verdict line shown when the learner picks a trap (e.g. 'That's the trap').

correctLabel.description: Prefix used when the surviving answer is revealed, e.g. 'Survives:'.

Ret_ForensicAudit.name: Forensic Audit
Ret_ForensicAudit.description: Clickable code lines, essay paragraphs, or balance sheet rows where the learner hunts down the error.

schema.title: Ret_ForensicAudit
schema.description: Clickable code lines, essay paragraphs, or balance sheet rows where the learner hunts down the error.

artifactType.description: What kind of artifact the learner is auditing; drives default line labels and styling.

brief.description: Short instruction to the learner: what to hunt for.

artifactLabel.description: Optional caption for the artifact card (e.g. 'client_loop.py — extract').

lines.description: The artifact, one clickable line/row at a time, in order.

label.description: Optional line number / row label / paragraph marker.

secondary.description: Optional right-hand column value (amount, tag, comment).

isError.description: True if this is the line the learner must find.

explanation.description: Feedback shown when this line is selected (why it is wrong, or why it is clean).

maxMisses.description: Optional number of incorrect clicks allowed before the correct line is revealed. Default: unlimited.

revealLabel.description: Optional label for the reveal button that appears after maxMisses is reached.

completionMessage.description: Optional message shown once the error line is found.

Ret_InterleavedMatrix.name: Interleaved Matrix
Ret_InterleavedMatrix.description: Cross-topic comparative grids mixing past units, filled in cell by cell.

schema.title: Interleaved Matrix
schema.description: A cross-topic comparative grid the learner fills in cell by cell from memory, interleaving material from several past units.

matrixSubtitle.description: Optional short line under the heading, e.g. the units being interleaved.

rows.description: The grid's row headers, one per comparative dimension or concept.

label.description: Row header text shown in the leftmost column.

sourceUnit.description: Optional unit tag shown small under the row label.

columns.description: The grid's column headers, one per topic/unit being compared.

label.description: Column header text shown at the top of the column.

sourceUnit.description: Optional unit tag shown small under the column label.

cells.description: Answer key: one entry per row/column intersection that the learner must fill.

rowId.description: The row this cell belongs to.

colId.description: The column this cell belongs to.

answer.description: The canonical answer the learner is retrieving.

placeholder.description: Optional hint shown as the input placeholder for this cell.

feedback.description: Optional short feedback shown after the cell is correctly filled.

completionMessage.description: Optional message shown once every cell is filled correctly.

Ret_FarTransferWorkbench.name: Far Transfer Workbench
Ret_FarTransferWorkbench.description: An unfamiliar real-world scenario (medical, aerospace, legal, business) that the learner solves by applying the rule.

schema.title: Ret_FarTransferWorkbench
schema.description: An unfamiliar real-world scenario solved by applying a rule: the learner reads the scenario brief and composes the decision/answer plus the reasoning step that applies the rule, then submits for targeted feedback.

eyebrow.description: Short domain label shown above the scenario title (e.g. 'AEROSPACE — FLIGHT OPERATIONS').

scenarioTitle.description: Headline of the unfamiliar real-world situation.

scenarioBody.description: Narrative of the unfamiliar scenario the learner must solve.

contextItems.description: Optional hard facts of the situation (numbers, constraints, dates). Rendered as a tight facts strip.

rule.description: The rule/ principle the learner must transfer to this unfamiliar situation.

name.description: Short rule name, e.g. 'Conservation of Mechanical Energy'.

statement.description: The rule itself as learned in the original (familiar) context.

decisionPrompt.description: The one question the learner must answer from the scenario.

decisionPlaceholder.description: Optional placeholder for the decision textarea.

rationalePrompt.description: Prompt for the brief reasoning step that applies the rule (e.g. 'Cite the rule step that justifies it').

rationalePlaceholder.description: Optional placeholder for the reasoning textarea.

referenceNote.description: Optional short note on the deck/policy/exam sheet the learner may lean on.

targetAnswer.description: The correct transfer solution used for scoring and feedback.

rationale.description: Model reasoning that shows the rule applied.

decisionKeywords.description: Phrases expected in a correct decision; used to score the decision field.

rationaleKeywords.description: Phrases showing the rule genuinely applied in this new situation; used to score the reasoning field.

misconception.description: Targeted feedback shown when the reasoning does not carry the rule.

detail.description: What is wrong and how to fix the reasoning.

rubric.description: Optional scoring dimensions shown as the submission checklist.

submitLabel.description: Optional label for the submit button (default 'Lock in decision').

retryLabel.description: Optional label for the revise button after feedback (default 'Revise the memo').

nextLabel.description: Optional label for the done-confirmation button (default 'Case closed').

Ret_ReverseSyllogism.name: Reverse Syllogism
Ret_ReverseSyllogism.description: Given a conclusion or an error, select the missing false premise.

schema.title: Ret_ReverseSyllogism
schema.description: Reverse syllogism drill: given a conclusion or an error, the learner selects the missing false premise from a set of candidates.

title.description: Block heading shown at the top.

subtitle.description: Optional short supporting line under the title.

conclusionLabel.description: Label for the conclusion/error block, e.g. 'The Error on the Page'.

conclusion.description: The conclusion or error statement the learner must explain by finding the hidden false premise.

prompt.description: Instruction line telling the learner what to select.

candidates.description: Candidate premises; exactly one should be flagged correct.

text.description: The premise statement shown to the learner.

correct.description: True for the missing false premise that actually produces the conclusion.

feedback.description: Shown after a selection: why this premise does or does not yield the conclusion.

revealHeading.description: Heading for the feedback panel after an answer, e.g. 'The Missing Premise'.

revealExplain.description: Full worked reconstruction of the syllogism shown after an answer.

streakLabel.description: Label for the streak counter, e.g. 'Streak'.

resetLabel.description: Accessible label for the try-again button, e.g. 'Try another conclusion'.

Ret_DialCalibrator.name: Dial Calibrator
Ret_DialCalibrator.description: A dial the learner tunes to bring variables into safe tolerance zones.

schema.title: Ret_DialCalibrator payload
schema.description: Content payload for the Ret_DialCalibrator retention block: a dial the learner tunes to bring a measured variable into a safe tolerance zone.

title.description: Heading shown at the top of the block, e.g. a lab or skill name.

taskPrompt.description: One-line instruction telling the learner what to tune and why (no question phrasing).

variableLabel.description: Name of the physical quantity being tuned, e.g. 'Applied Force'.

unit.description: Unit suffix rendered after the numeric readout, e.g. 'N', 'rad/s', 'mL'.

minValue.description: Lower bound of the dial's range.

maxValue.description: Upper bound of the dial's range.

step.description: Smallest increment the dial may land on; also drives arrow-key and long-press increments.

targetValue.description: Centre of the safe tolerance zone.

tolerance.description: Plus/minus half-width of the safe zone; |value - targetValue| <= tolerance counts as in-tolerance.

safeZoneLabel.description: Short label drawn inside the tolerance arc, e.g. 'SAFE OPERATING RANGE'.

startValue.description: Initial dial value when the block first renders.

onTargetMessage.description: Optional confirmation message shown once the dial is inside tolerance.

outOfRangeMessage.description: Optional hint shown while the dial is outside tolerance.

variableLabelShort.description: Optional abbreviated label for tight mobile layouts; falls back to variableLabel.
